### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via AgentSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82e45276aecdf63c2ba6909f192e7e0da49cd5e6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cfdae7e7853632b63d4990b6ea24a035609c43c4` — the merge of head `0f2b445958baa378f4179b32c959f22f2a248237` into base `82e45276aecdf63c2ba6909f192e7e0da49cd5e6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cfdae7e7853632b63d4990b6ea24a035609c43c4 && git checkout cfdae7e7853632b63d4990b6ea24a035609c43c4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82e45276aecdf63c2ba6909f192e7e0da49cd5e6 0f2b445958baa378f4179b32c959f22f2a248237 && git checkout -B drift-repro 82e45276aecdf63c2ba6909f192e7e0da49cd5e6 && git merge --no-ff 0f2b445958baa378f4179b32c959f22f2a248237

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82e45276aecdf63c2ba6909f192e7e0da49cd5e6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82e45276aecdf63c2ba6909f192e7e0da49cd5e6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0f2b445958baa378f4179b32c959f22f2a248237`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/agent.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts + none

No other file in the diff implements or enforces the two `hits` files: `agent.test.ts`, the regenerated `content/docs/references/ai/agent.mdx`, the eleven `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` bundles and the changeset are tests, generated output and a changeset, the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Read to judge, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/agent.json`, and the first consumer, cloud `packages/service-ai/src/ai-service.ts`, `routes/agent-routes.ts` and `eval/eval-runner.ts` at cloud b2b7b07.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set of `AgentSchema.planning.maxIterations`: `int().min(1).max(100).default(10)` becomes `int().min(1).max(1000).default(10)`. Whole numbers 101 to 1000 are newly accepted. Nothing accepted on `main` is refused: 1 to 100 parse as before, 0, negatives, non-integers and non-numbers are refused as before, and the refusal for a too-large value moves from 101 to 1001. Right: a pure widening.
- Default: 10, unchanged. An agent that omits the key, or omits `planning`, behaves as before. Right.
- Aliases (`maxSteps`, `maxLoops`, `iterations`, `maxTurns`) and the strict `planning` object: untouched by the diff. Right.
- Published JSON schema: `maximum` moves 100 to 1000 and `description` takes the new `.describe()` text. The schema directory is not in the diff (regenerated at build); `Build Core` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are green on the head. Right.
- Public prose surface: the `.describe()` string, the reference row in `agent.mdx`, the Studio help text for `planning` in `agent.form.ts` and its eleven translations. Each stated or implied 1–100 on `main`; each now states 1–1000. No exported symbol, type or signature changes: the inferred type of `maxIterations` is still `number`. Right.
- No other reader in this repo assumes 100 or less. `git grep maxIterations` on the head finds, outside the diff, only the flow loop node's own key (`LoopConfig.maxIterations`, a different schema with its own ceiling), `ChatWithToolsOptions.maxIterations` (no bound), the liveness row (no bound) and UI code that names or displays the key. No clamp exists in the framework; the PR body's table agrees with the tree on every row I re-read.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right. The diff widens the accept set of a published, authorable schema key and takes nothing away; the closed arm `(widening)` is the correct one, and the line is present and identical in the PR body and the changeset body.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` is right. AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3: an accepted value a metadata author could not write before is `added`. It is not `narrowed` (no value is refused that was accepted) and not `semantic`: the default is unchanged and the runtime meaning is unchanged, since the docblock now describes what the consumer already did (one model call plus its tool batch per iteration); only the description moved.
- Level: the kind `added` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. The diff moves `@objectstack/spec` (schema and form) and `@objectstack/platform-objects` (the translation bundles it ships); the changeset declares `minor` on both. Right, and neither is over-declared: both sit in the one `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`, so the release level is the same either way. No `major`, no BREAKING banner owed.
- ADR-0087: no entry owed. That disposition is for a breaking changeset; nothing an author wrote before is refused or changes meaning, so there is nothing to convert, and the changeset says "Nothing to migrate". Triage left this to review ("add the ADR-0087 entry if the review asks for one"): the review does not ask for one.
- Gate verdicts on the head: `Check Changeset` success (both runs), `Lint · repo & tooling gates` success, `Spec property liveness` success, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in both reports. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, "`Clause-②` written with the closed arm `yes (widening)`": accepted; it is the form AGENTS.md prescribes, and the card's free text means the same.
- Deviation, "`agent.form.ts` touched": accepted, and required. Its help text stated "(1–100, default 10)"; left alone it would contradict the schema it describes. It is a `hits` file and is judged in ④.
- Deviation, "platform-objects translation bundles touched": accepted. `en` is the regenerated mirror of the form help text and `check:i18n` reds without it; the ten translated values stated 1–100 and would have been false. I checked all eleven on the head: each states 1–1000 and none retains 1–100. The wording of the ten is the lane seat's remainder; the dev's own note that a native-speaker pass is welcome stands as a non-blocking follow-up.
- Deviation, "review request to the maintainer not sent": a hand-off step for the dispatching seat, no contract effect.
- Bound choice (1000, where the card says "at least 300, or remove the upper bound"): inside the card's ruling, not a re-ruling. The maintainer's word fixes the value cloud declares (300), and the card leaves the ceiling to the implementer above that floor. Judged on its merits in ④.
- Claim comment drift: the claim first said `Metadata-protocol: none` and was corrected to `added` one minute later by the same seat; the PR body and changeset carry `added`. Consistent on the head.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. The diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Security: none found; the dev reports none. A larger fuse raises the worst-case cost of one turn, but only for an author who writes it, and the consumer's time limit and token budget still stop a round before it starts (`governor.limitReached()` at the top of each iteration).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts`** — against the card's ruling and the first consumer.

- The ruling asks for: the bound raised to at least 300, `int().min(1)` kept, and a docblock saying the value is a runaway fuse counted in model calls (one call plus its tool batch), not a quality knob. The tree does all three, and the card's acceptance (`AgentSchema.parse` accepts 300) is pinned by the new test.
- The docblock against the consumer. cloud `AIService.chatWithTools` runs a counted `for` loop from 0 up to, and not including, `maxIterations`; each pass makes exactly one model call and, if that call requests tools, runs the batch and loops. `routes/agent-routes.ts` and `eval/eval-runner.ts` pass `agent.planning?.maxIterations` straight in, with no clamp and no upper assumption, so a declared 300 or 1000 is honoured as written. "One iteration is one model call plus the batch of tool calls it requests" is true sentence for sentence. "Not a quality knob, and raising it does not make the agent reason better" is true: the value is read nowhere but the loop condition.
- "No value can switch the fuse off" holds: the ceiling is finite and `min(1)` forbids 0. Tried to break it: a string, a float, 0, 1001 and `Infinity` are all refused by `number().int().min(1).max(1000)`; the aliases resolve to the same key before the same check.
- 1000 against 300 and against no ceiling. A ceiling of exactly 300 would make the maintainer's ruled value the maximum, so the next calibration upward would be another published-contract change; no ceiling would let one typo disable the fuse, which is the one thing the key is for. 1000 keeps the published `maximum` for form renderers and leaves room above the surveyed values (300, 500). The choice holds. It is also the cheaper direction to be wrong in: a later raise is another widening, while a later cut would be a narrowing.
- The first consumer's own default is still 10 (`DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS`) and its agents still declare 100 or less; nothing in cloud breaks when the pin moves, and cloud#5029 then declares 300. The seam the card names (spec bound to `AgentRuntime.loadAgent` parse) is closed by this diff alone.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/agent.form.ts`** — against the schema it describes.

- The help text now reads "a runaway fuse counted in model calls, each one model call plus its tool batch, after which the agent stops (1–1000, default 10)". The range and the default agree with the schema on the head, and the unit agrees with the docblock. The field stays `type: 'composite'` on `planning`, whose only key is `maxIterations`, so describing the one key as the composite's help is accurate.

Findings:

- N1 (nit) — "counted in model calls" and "after which the agent stops" are slightly loose against the consumer. When the fuse is reached, cloud makes one more model call without tools to force a final answer, and a structured-output retry is a model round that does not count against the value (the consumer's own comment says the key "bounds TOOL rounds"). So a turn can make a few more model calls than the number written. The docblock's own definition of an iteration is exact, the wording is the one the ruling dictates, and the fuse property (the loop always ends) is unaffected. Left as an accepted deviation; if the wording is ever tightened, "counted in tool rounds" is the precise unit.
- N2 (nit) — `ChatWithToolsOptions.maxIterations` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts` (outside the diff, read only) still says "Maximum number of tool call loop iterations (default: 10)" with no fuse wording. It states no bound and is not wrong. No action in this PR.

No must-fix, no should-fix.
